plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win), which means the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay, since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own. There's no benefit to shading my bid up or down in this format. My value is $36, so I will bid $36.

This is a second-price auction (Vickrey auction) where I pay the second-highest bid if I win. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. With a value of $8, I should bid exactly $8.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win. Bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $44.
